packs.description: Delivery workflow router: codebase-driven implementation, planning, testing, shipping, prototyping, or development lifecycle work. Loads matching leaf skill on demand.
Foundations router: reusable proven code from indexed inspiration repositories, encoded as skills so future work stacks shortcuts instead of re-deriving them.
Code quality and reliability router: refactoring, code review, cleanup, deep module design, defense in depth, deprecation, fallow analysis, performance, root-cause, type standards.
Research and discovery router: web search, documentation lookup, package source inspection, deep-context study, adversarial review, PDF extraction.
Platform and delivery-infrastructure router: CI/CD, Cloudflare, Vercel deployment, Git workflow, worktrees.
Authoring and documentation router: writing or editing skills, documentation, ADRs, API and interface design.

_descriptions.development-lifecycle: Use when planning a project lifecycle, milestones, or development phases.
_descriptions.incremental-implementation: Use when implementing any feature or refactor touching more than one file.
_descriptions.planning-and-task-breakdown: Use when breaking a goal into tasks, estimating, or sequencing work.
_descriptions.prototype: Use when building a throwaway prototype or validating an idea.
_descriptions.shipping-and-launch: Use when shipping, releasing, launching, or productionizing.
_descriptions.source-driven-development: Use when shipping code that depends on unfamiliar libraries, external APIs, or framework behavior; cite the source or mark the decision unverified.
_descriptions.spec-driven-development: Use when a run is expected to last 4-10 days or span multiple sessions, requirements stay ambiguous after code inspection, or a durable cross-team contract is required.
_descriptions.codebase-driven-development: Use when starting any implementation work: code is the ground truth, one-shot with examples, and escalate to a spec only when the run outlives the session.
_descriptions.code-foundations: Use when a proven code pattern, primitive, or integration is worth reusing: encode it as a skill so future work reuses the shortcut.
